sections.html: Franklin County is where Pasco, the seat and biggest city, anchors the Tri-Cities alongside Kennewick and Richland, which are in neighboring Benton County. The 2020 count was 96,749 residents, up from 78,163 in 2010. The county held 29,740 housing units in 2020, with 3.3% vacant, and 68.3% of occupied homes were owned by their occupants. Four cities (Pasco, Connell, Mesa and Kahlotus) make up the incorporated area, so your tax code area and local excise rate depend on where the house sits.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Franklin County?
sections.html:
Property tax here passes through three desks. One sets values (Assessor), one rules on disputes (Board of Equalization), and one sends the bill and takes your money (Treasurer). The first two share the courthouse at 1016 N 4th Avenue, Pasco.

  • Assessor: Room A-104 in the basement. Call 509-545-3506. Open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Board of Equalization: Room A102. Phone 509-546-5855 weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., or email boeclerk@franklincountywa.gov.
  • Treasurer: collects both installments and runs the county's tax sales. Online account tools, a drive-up drop box and a paperless billing portal are offered.

Do not expect the Assessor to explain your rate or send a bill. The rate comes from voters, state limits and each taxing district's assessed value, and the Treasurer does the billing.

sections.h2: How often is a Franklin County house revalued?
sections.html:
A county appraiser must physically visit each parcel no less than every six years. In between, values are refreshed countywide every year using statistical analysis of sales. When comparable homes in an area keep selling above or below their assessed values, that area's roll is adjusted. A remodel, an addition or a subdivision earns a fresh value.

Real property is valued each January 1 for the following year's taxes (RCW 84.40.020). The mailing calendar runs like this: Change of Value Notices in the third quarter, tax statements in February. Since a summer notice looks back at last year's market, a fast change in prices may not be reflected yet.

Appraisers rely on sales comparison and cost for most homes, and the income approach mostly for business property. Pull your record before listing and check square footage, bedrooms and heating type against the house itself. A single wrong entry can move the value either way.

Two installments are due, April 30 and October 31. Charges for lateness are added on the first of each month. Skip the first half and the entire year's tax goes delinquent, so interest runs on everything. Statements can fall on a weekend: October 31, 2026 was a Saturday, so ask the Treasurer how a Monday payment is treated in a year like that.

Property typeInterestPenalties
Residential, four units or fewer, taxes levied 2023 or later9% a year, charged monthlyNone
All other real property, personal property12% a year, charged monthly3% on June 1 and a further 8% on December 1

The rates come from RCW 84.56.020, and the Assessor posts the June 1 and December 1 dates on its important dates page.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Franklin County assessment?
sections.html:
Your first move is to contact the Assessor, either by phone at 509-545-3506 or in Room A-104. Review how the value was figured, and ask the appraiser to line it up against recent sales nearby or to inspect the house. Still unhappy? The next step is a taxpayer petition to the Board of Equalization.

Your petition has to be mailed by July 1 of the assessment year or 30 days after the notice date, depending on which comes later. When that day is a weekend or holiday, you get the next business day. A postmark on or before the last day counts for mail. One form covers one parcel only.

Appraisals, maps, photos and letters must be submitted 21 days ahead of the hearing. The Board assumes the Assessor is correct, and under WAC 458-14-046 you must meet a standard of clear, cogent and convincing evidence to change that. If your proof is not ready, file a protective appeal before the cutoff to hold your place. Board sessions have run from October into January in recent cycles.

The Assessor lists several state programs. Each begins with a call to 509-545-3506.

  • Exemptions for senior citizens and disabled persons.
  • Exemptions for qualifying nonprofit property.
  • A destroyed property claim, which adjusts the value of damaged buildings.
  • A historical restoration exemption for significant property under restoration.
  • Open space classification for agricultural land, timberland and nature preserves.

Nonprofit exemption applications must reach the Department of Revenue by March 31. Farm open space applications are treated as approved on May 1 unless the Assessor says otherwise.

Phone payments ended on January 1, 2024. Pay through the online portal, mail a check, or walk in. A drive-up drop box sits under the blue banner across from the security building.

Sign up for email reminders each April and October on the paperless tax bill page, and staff will help you set up the account. The office also offers several payment plan options, so call before an account slips far behind. To change an address, use the Assessor's page after confirming the address with the postal service.

If a parcel goes to tax sale, the county advertises it at least three weeks ahead in the Franklin County Graphic and the Tri-City Herald. State law lets the treasurer foreclose on parcels with unpaid taxes, so an old balance is worth clearing early.

sections.h2: What you owe when you sell
sections.html:
When a Washington house sells, real estate excise tax follows, normally at the seller's expense. Payment goes to the treasurer of the county that holds the property and is owed as of the sale date, even if the deed is recorded later. After a month, interest and penalties begin.

State rates come from a sliding scale at the Department of Revenue, with price breaks at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000 starting January 1, 2027. Your town adds its own local rate. The Treasurer or your closing agent can quote the combined figure for Pasco or the town where you live.

If property tax is still owed, request a payoff figure from the Treasurer and pay it out of closing proceeds so the buyer gets clean title. Buyers who pay cash skip a lender's appraisal and underwriting, which removes steps that often slow a closing. For a quick sale, line up the payoff number, the excise tax and the deed paperwork before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: When are Franklin County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Installments fall on April 30 and October 31. Miss the first and the full year is delinquent, with interest or penalties on the entire amount.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Franklin County property value?
faqs.a: Talk to the Assessor at 509-545-3506 first. If that does not resolve it, petition the Board of Equalization by the later of July 1 or 30 days after the notice. The clerk's number is 509-546-5855.

faqs.q: Can I pay Franklin County property tax by phone?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer stopped taking phone payments on January 1, 2024. Use the online portal, mail, the counter or the drive-up drop box.

faqs.q: How often does Franklin County inspect homes?
faqs.a: At least once every six years in person. Values are also updated every year across the county through analysis of sales.

faqs.q: Who pays excise tax when you sell in Franklin County?
faqs.a: Normally the seller. The tax goes to the county treasurer and is owed on the sale date, combining a price-based state rate with a local rate.
